newsitem.title: USA: U.S. attache--India 97/98 wheat imports 3-5 mln T.
newsitem.headline: U.S. attache--India 97/98 wheat imports 3-5 mln T.

text.p: An agricultural attache posted at the U.S. embassy in New Delhi forecast India would import three million to five million tonnes of wheat during 1997/98. The attache said high wheat prices, dwindling government stocks, record consumption, stagnant production of rice and coarse grains, current wheat crop expectations, population growth, rising incomes, and limited wheat procurement boosting policy options pointed to continued imports during 1997/98.

"Given current crop expectations, India is expected to import 3-5 mmt of wheat to keep domestic prices at bay and augment government stocks of wheat," the attache wrote in a report released in Washington this week.
Attache reports are not official USDA data.

The attache noted India wheat consumption has risen dramatically in the past two years. He said estimated 1996/97 consumption exceeded 1996 production by 3.4 million tonnes and predicted consumption would outpace production during 1997/98 unless there was a very good 1997 harvest. "What India needs to avert imports in 1997/98 is a 69 or 70 mmt crop (7 percent above the previous record) which would push production higher than anticipated consumption. We would describe this as a fantastic crop and at this stage a crop of this size seems unlikely," he wrote.
USDA has forecast India 1996/97 wheat imports at 2.0 million tonnes.
